mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to recover from its current low base, then weekday trips will spill into nearby retail and recreation within four weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC upward versus the prior month. The signal fails if WORKPLACES stalls or reverses before a further weekly increase appears.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not become less negative over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES increasing again for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL time indicates people are spending more hours outside home, and that should translate into higher discretionary retail visits over the next one to two weeks. The mechanism breaks if RESIDENTIAL rises again while RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls.
failure_condition: Over the next 14 days, RETAIL_REC remains below its current weekly level even though RESIDENTIAL declines further or stays below the present reading.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points from one week to the next while WORKPLACES is also rising, the combined recovery in commuting access and job attendance will lift retail activity over the next four weeks. This fails when transit rebounds without a matching workplace recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 5 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES rises in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last 28 days after a week in which TRANSIT rises by 5+ points and WORKPLACES also rises.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PARKS mobility signals warmer-weather outdoor substitution that diverts some leisure trips away from indoor shopping, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next month. The effect should weaken if park mobility falls back quickly.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its current weekly level by more than 10 points and stays elevated for 2 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining elevated for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When grocery and pharmacy trips remain elevated, households are consolidating errands and limiting discretionary shopping, which keeps retail-and-recreation mobility below the prior four-week mean over the next one to two weeks. The mechanism fails if grocery mobility normalizes without any retail rebound.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays at or below its current elevated level.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise, that combination indicates a broad return to outside-home routines that should raise RETAIL_REC within four weeks. The signal fails when only one mobility stream improves and the other two do not move together.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each rise in the same two-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move above its last-28-day mean after a two-week period in which RESIDENTIAL falls and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise.

mechanism_narrative: During a tightening regime, a renewed drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES will precede weaker retail footfall as commuting and office-linked shopping fade. Over the next month this should push RETAIL_REC lower than its recent four-week average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC becomes less negative over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declining together.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS remains volatile while GROCERY_PHARM stays stable, the mobility mix implies outdoor leisure substitution without a broad consumer rebound, so retail-and-recreation should remain weak over the next week. The hypothesis fails if retail improves even though parks activity is still choppy and grocery trips do not strengthen.
candidate_trigger: PARKS changes by more than 10 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM stays within 2 points of its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days despite volatile PARKS and nearly unchanged GROCERY_PHARM.
